skill.summary: Build authenticated Azure Queue Storage workflows for queue management, message processing, retries, encoding, and SAS access.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 87 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, expected Azure endpoints, named environment variables, and standard Base64 decoding. These examples do not execute shell commands, read environment files, or send credentials to unrelated services. One medium concern remains: the account SAS example grants broad permissions across all resource types for 24 hours.

remediation.issue: The account SAS example grants broad permissions and resource access for 24 hours.
remediation.suggestion: Use only required permissions and resource types, narrow the scope, and shorten the token lifetime.

content.user_title: Build Azure Queue Workflows in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure Queue Storage integrations require careful authentication and message lifecycle handling. This skill provides TypeScript patterns for queue administration, processing, retries, encoding, SAS access, and errors.
actual_capabilities: Configures queue clients with identity credentials, connection strings, shared keys, or SAS tokens.
Creates, lists, inspects, updates, and deletes Azure storage queues.
Sends, receives, peeks, updates, deletes, and clears queue messages.
Designs workers with visibility timeouts, retries, poison queues, and batch processing.
Explains message encoding, SAS generation, SDK errors, types, and service limits.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not deploy or operate Azure resources.
Users must supply an Azure account, credentials, permissions, and runtime configuration.
Examples require testing for application-specific reliability, idempotency, monitoring, and security requirements.
Some authentication and SAS features work only in Node.js.

use_cases.title: Create a Queue Client
use_cases.description: Configure secure Azure Queue Storage access and select the correct authentication method.

use_cases.title: Build a Reliable Worker
use_cases.description: Implement message polling, visibility renewal, deletion, retry limits, and poison queue handling.

use_cases.title: Review Queue Operations
use_cases.description: Check SDK methods, service limits, error handling, and platform compatibility before release.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript QueueServiceClient using DefaultAzureCredential and validate the required account name.

prompt_templates.title: Process Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a worker that receives ten messages, handles each safely, and deletes only successful messages.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Repeated Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Add retry limits and a poison queue while preserving message content and avoiding premature deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production worker with visibility renewal, idempotency, bounded concurrency, least-privilege access, observability, and graceful shutdown.

output_examples.input: Create a worker that receives messages in batches and removes successful items.
output: A worker flow receives up to ten messages with a bounded visibility timeout.
Successful messages are deleted with their current pop receipts.
Failed messages remain available for retry and move to a poison queue after the limit.

output_examples.input: Recommend authentication for a Node.js service running in Azure.
output_examples.output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with the storage account URL and a managed identity that has only the required queue role.

output_examples.input: Plan support for a task that may run longer than the visibility timeout.
output_examples.output: Renew visibility before expiry, retain the latest pop receipt, stop the timer after processing, and delete only after successful completion.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity and DefaultAzureCredential over shared keys or long-lived connection strings.
Use idempotent processing, bounded retries, and a poison queue for repeated failures.
Set visibility timeouts from observed processing duration and renew them for long tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not delete a message before its work completes successfully.
Do not grant broad SAS permissions or expose SAS URLs in logs.
Do not run an unbounded polling loop without backoff, cancellation, and monitoring.

faq.question: Which Azure package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the @azure/storage-queue package and uses @azure/identity for identity-based authentication.

faq.question: Which authentication method is preferred?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity when the deployment environment supports it.

faq.question: Can this skill create and delete queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents queue creation, listing, properties, metadata, and deletion operations.

faq.question: How are failed messages handled?
faq.answer: Use dequeue counts, bounded retries, and a separate poison queue for messages that repeatedly fail.

faq.question: Does it support browser applications?
faq.answer: Basic queue operations and SAS access work in browsers, but shared keys, SAS generation, and DefaultAzureCredential are Node.js features.

faq.question: Does the skill execute Azure operations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, and users must run and validate the resulting application in their own environment.
